items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and follow the codebase style (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookieAttribute, consistentHashIR, constructConsistentHash, mergeConsistentHash). API fields have doc comments. Formatted with gofmt.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: separate consistent_hash.go, IR wired into constructor/plugin, merge registered. But mergeConsistentHash spans merge.go#L625-L678 (~53 lines), so it does not look like short single-purpose helpers shared by build and merge. Types also sit in a new file, not traffic_policy_types.go.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Input checks are at the boundary: MinLength=1 on keys and a CEL rule for disable exclusivity. I couldn't see how a bad cookie ttl string fails, since the implementation was omitted. Substitution is optional while the reference requires it. Hidden tests all pass.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: Golden /merged route lists the higher-priority X-Shared-Header first, then x-route-header, cookie, queryParameter, filterState, so canonical order holds. Metadata records consistentHash for both policies. mergeConsistentHash is registered in merge.go. F2P passes.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: Golden /empty route gets exactly one hash policy, connectionProperties.sourceIp: true. The /disabled route gets no hashPolicy. A CEL rule on ConsistentHash ('when disable is true, no other consistentHash fields may be set') is in the generated CRD.
